# Mneme HQ

> Mneme HQ is the open-source decision and control layer for agentic software development. It turns approved engineering decisions into agent context, deterministic enforcement, and inspectable enforcement results across AI coding agents, repositories, and CI workflows. Architecture is the first decision domain: Mneme prevents architectural drift by enforcing approved ADRs and engineering standards before incompatible changes land.

## What Mneme is

- Category: the decision and control layer for agentic software development.
- Value: make engineering decisions portable, enforceable, and inspectable across AI coding agents, repositories, and CI workflows.
- Current product: Mneme starts with architecture. ADR-based decisions, applicability (which decisions apply to a change), deterministic rules, agent context, and guide, warn, or block verdicts traced to the source decision.
- First use case: prevent architectural drift before AI-generated code ships.

Architecture is the first decision domain. The decision model is designed to extend to broader engineering policy, but dedicated security, platform, and compliance decision domains are not shipped today (security-relevant patterns can already be written as repository rules); see https://mnemehq.com/roadmap/.

Mneme does not replace your coding agent, CI system, policy engine, or code review. It supplies the approved decisions that supported agents and CI gates check changes against. Governance is an outcome of Mneme, not its category name.

## Category positioning

Rules files document standards. Mneme enforces them.
Memory tools recall context. Mneme governs implementation.
RAG retrieves knowledge. Mneme operationalizes decisions.

## How Mneme fits the AI coding stack

Pre-generation enforcement of approved decisions is Mneme. Generation and runtime are agent frameworks and runtime harnesses such as Cursor, Claude Code, and managed agent platforms. Post-generation observability is tools like SentRux. SentRux tells you when the agent violated architecture. Mneme helps prevent the violation from being proposed in the first place. The two layers are complementary.

## Enterprise framing

Mneme runs inside existing engineering workflows, including Azure and GitHub-based environments. The same decision corpus reaches supported coding agents through agent hooks and generated editor rules, local pre-commit checks, and CI gates, and each verdict is traced to the decision that produced it.

## Architecture

Five stages. No vector store. No ML.
project_memory.json into MemoryStore into Retriever into ContextBuilder into LLMAdapter into Evaluator. Retrieval is deterministic keyword scoring. Same query returns the same result every time.

## Compare pages

Structured comparisons between Mneme HQ and alternative approaches — for engineering teams actively evaluating governance tools.

- [Compare hub](https://mnemehq.com/compare/): Index of all comparison pages with the decision template each one follows.
- [Mneme HQ vs CodeRabbit](https://mnemehq.com/compare/coderabbit/): CodeRabbit reviews code after it's written. Mneme HQ enforces architectural constraints before generation.
- [Mneme HQ vs Cursor Rules](https://mnemehq.com/compare/cursor-rules/): Cursor Rules are plain-text suggestions. Mneme HQ is structured enforcement with a precedence engine and hook-level blocking.
- [Mneme HQ vs Claude Code Memory](https://mnemehq.com/compare/claude-code-memory/): Claude Code memory provides instructions the model may follow. Mneme HQ hooks into operations and blocks violations.
- [Mneme HQ vs CLAUDE.md](https://mnemehq.com/compare/claude-md/): Advisory context files vs deterministic precedence and hook-level enforcement.
- [Mneme HQ vs GitHub Copilot](https://mnemehq.com/compare/github-copilot/): GitHub Copilot generates code; Mneme HQ enforces architectural boundaries deterministically.
- [Mneme HQ vs Windsurf](https://mnemehq.com/compare/windsurf/): Windsurf Cascade agentic flows paired with deterministic edit-time governance.
- [Mneme HQ vs Aider](https://mnemehq.com/compare/aider/): Terminal AI pair programming paired with shared architectural constraints.
- [Mneme HQ vs Continue.dev](https://mnemehq.com/compare/continue-dev/): Open-source IDE assistant paired with typed decision precedence.
- [Mneme HQ vs Sourcegraph Cody](https://mnemehq.com/compare/sourcegraph-cody/): Codebase-aware context retrieval paired with edit-time constraint enforcement.
- [Devin vs Architectural Governance](https://mnemehq.com/compare/devin-vs-architectural-governance/): Devin executes work; Mneme deterministically governs architectural boundaries.
- [Google Antigravity vs Mneme](https://mnemehq.com/compare/google-antigravity-vs-mneme/): Agent execution & orchestration environments paired with architectural governance.
- [RAG Coding Memory vs Mneme](https://mnemehq.com/compare/rag-coding-memory/): Contextual memory vs exact deterministic decision memory.
- [Mneme HQ vs RAG-based Governance](https://mnemehq.com/compare/rag-vs-governance/): Probabilistic vector search vs deterministic constraint enforcement.

## Integration pages

How Mneme HQ fits into the tools engineering teams already use. The local MCP server is an interoperability boundary for Mneme's decision layer; enforcement integrations continue to provide deterministic protection in editor and CI workflows.

- [Integrate Mneme](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/): Canonical integration entry point. Choose local MCP for agent interoperability, the CLI for repository and CI enforcement, or the Python package for custom adapters and embedded workflows; then select the validated coding-agent or CI boundary.
- [Model Context Protocol integration](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/mcp/): Discovery guide to Mneme's local stdio MCP server, its decision retrieval and proposal capabilities, and the authority boundary that keeps acceptance and enforcement outside MCP.
- [Claude Code integration](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/claude-code/): Hook-level enforcement for every Edit, Write, and MultiEdit Claude Code attempts.
- [Cursor integration](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/cursor/): Mneme HQ as the authoritative corpus behind Cursor Rules sessions.
- [GitHub Actions integration](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/github-actions/): CI enforcement gate — block PRs that violate architectural decisions before they merge.
- [ADR import integration](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/adr-import/): Import an existing ADR corpus into Mneme's enforcement pipeline. Add a Constraints section to any ADR, run one command to preview, one to apply — decisions become live guardrails without rewriting your ADRs.
- [Perplexity Enterprise](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/perplexity/): Research & analysis assistant. Works alongside, not a native integration. Perplexity helps teams understand why. Mneme helps teams preserve what must remain true. Workflow pattern: research in Perplexity → record decision in Mneme → enforce across every coding agent. Closes the gap between research rationale and governance constraint. No API handshake — the integration is the discipline.
- [Claude Agent SDK integration](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/claude-agent-sdk/): Mneme as the governance/runtime policy layer for Claude Agent SDK workflows. Claude Agent SDK handles execution and orchestration; Mneme handles architectural invariants and enforcement. Covers pre-execution governance hooks (intercept before tool calls), post-execution verification, enforcement traces in long-running agent loops, and CI gate integration. This is an infrastructure-shaped relationship: SDK = execution layer, Mneme = enforcement layer.

## Machine-readable agent discovery

Use these endpoints to discover Mneme's agent-facing interfaces without scraping navigation or guessing an API shape.

- [AI Catalog](https://mnemehq.com/.well-known/ai-catalog.json): Typed index of Mneme's agent-facing discovery resources.
- [Integrate Mneme](https://mnemehq.com/integrations/): Human- and agent-readable starting point for MCP, CLI, Python package, and validated enforcement integrations.
- [Agent Skills index](https://mnemehq.com/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): Machine-readable index of published Mneme skills.
- [Mneme Decision MCP skill](https://mnemehq.com/.well-known/agent-skills/mneme-decision-mcp/SKILL.md): Installation, stdio host configuration, six-tool inventory, and authority boundary for Mneme's local Decision MCP server.
- [Decision MCP tool catalog](https://mnemehq.com/.well-known/mcp/decision-tools.json): Runtime-generated `tools/list` contract from the released mneme-hq 0.9.2 MCP server, including descriptions, JSON Schemas, annotations, and validated request examples.
- [Official MCP Registry record](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=io.github.MnemeHQ%2Fmneme): Canonical package discovery record for `io.github.MnemeHQ/mneme`.
- [MCP server metadata source](https://github.com/MnemeHQ/mneme/blob/main/server.json): Versioned `server.json` published to the official MCP Registry.

Mneme's released MCP interface is local and stdio-only. It does not expose a hosted HTTP/SSE endpoint, so the official MCP Registry package metadata is the canonical connection and installation contract; no remote MCP Server Card is advertised.

Official package identity: the official installable Mneme HQ distribution is [`mneme-hq` on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mneme-hq/) (`pip install mneme-hq`). Mneme HQ does not currently publish official npm packages. npm packages using the `@mnemehq` scope are not official Mneme HQ distributions.

## Reference docs

Operational and reference pages for engineers and buyers evaluating Mneme.

- [Works With](https://mnemehq.com/works-with/): Ecosystem compatibility surface. Model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, GLM, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Llama), coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Aider, Cline, OpenHands), agent frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents SDK), and deployment environments. Compatibility statements, not partnership claims; native integrations link through to /integrations/.
- [Platforms](https://mnemehq.com/platforms/): How Mneme runs inside enterprise developer platforms — Microsoft Azure & GitHub Enterprise, AWS Developer Environments, Google Cloud AI Engineering, and self-hosted / air-gapped. Focuses on CI/CD execution, agent/runtime governance, and policy enforcement in existing environments. Explicitly not cloud infrastructure provisioning, IAM, or Kubernetes setup. Answers the CTO question "will this fit into our Azure/GitHub/Copilot stack?" — yes, as the decision and control layer above the agents the platform runs.
- [Docs hub](https://mnemehq.com/docs/): Index of reference documentation — CLI, local MCP server, decision proposals, governance violations, protection activation, supported languages, and benchmark methodology.
- [CLI reference](https://mnemehq.com/docs/cli/): Reference for the `mneme` command-line interface, including the 0.9.0 `decision-mcp` server and human-authority `decision` commands alongside setup, audit, protection, enforcement, and integration workflows.
- [MCP server reference](https://mnemehq.com/docs/mcp/): Canonical operator documentation for installing the 0.9.0 MCP extra, starting the local stdio server, configuring proposal and ADR inputs, and using the frozen six-tool surface without crossing the human authority boundary.
- [Decision proposals](https://mnemehq.com/docs/decision-proposals/): The producer-to-proposal-to-human-review workflow, including `mneme decision proposals`, `show`, `accept`, and `reject`, materialization into canonical project memory, provenance, and current refresh limitations.
- [Decision model](https://mnemehq.com/docs/decision-model/): Mneme's core primitive is a durable engineering decision. Maps identity, applicability, authority, lifecycle, precedence, enforcement, and evidence to the pages that document each; architecture is the first decision domain.
- [Protection activation](https://mnemehq.com/docs/protection-activation/): How a Mneme-ready decision becomes a verified deterministic guardrail — mneme protect list, status, validate, activate. Validation is not activation; activation is explicit and idempotent; a decision only counts as Protected when a fresh canonical assessment observes real enforcement evidence. These commands have shipped in the released package since mneme-hq 0.7.0.
- [Governance violations](https://mnemehq.com/docs/governance-violations/): Twelve concrete examples of the architectural decisions Mneme enforces against, organized into five categories — architecture, workflow, security, dependency, and platform governance. Each example shows the rule, the AI's offending output, and the structured flags Mneme emits. Frames the category as decision injection, not lint scanning.
- [Supported languages (canonical docs)](https://mnemehq.com/docs/supported-languages/): Full coverage matrix. Python is Tier 1 production-grade with native CLI, benchmarks, hooks, and dogfooding. TypeScript and JavaScript are Tier 1 operationally supported (repo + dependency + workflow rules, no AST yet). Go, Java, C#, and Rust are Tier 2 — repo-level governance through architectural and dependency rules without ecosystem-specific policy packs. Includes the strategic positioning: repo-first, not parser-first.

## Reported benchmark

Governance Benchmark v1.1 methodology is published. The benchmark is deterministic and reproducible, measuring violation prevention rate, false positive rate, retrieval recall and precision, and the gap between end-to-end and oracle enforcement, across 36 scenarios in six categories including controls and ambiguous cases. Full results publish after scenario suite validation. Methodology and harness are public.
